summary: If the Kohen Gadol or the king sinned and then stepped down from his position, he still brings the same korban he would have brought before.

chunks.en: If the anointed Kohen sinned
chunks.st: In the case of an anointed priest who sinned
chunks.stMore: on the basis of his own erroneous halakhic ruling

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, who was anointed with special oil.

chunks.en: and afterwards stepped down from being the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and thereafter moved on from his anointment,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if he was disqualified due to a blemish that befell him before he brought his sin-offering,

chunks.en: and the same for a king who sinned
chunks.st: and likewise in the case of a king [nasi] who sinned

words.note: The Nasi here means the king.

chunks.en: and afterwards stepped down from his greatness,
chunks.st: and thereafter moved on from his prominence
chunks.stMore: before he had brought an offering,

chunks.en: the anointed Kohen brings a bull,
chunks.st: an anointed priest brings a bull
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he is no longer the High Priest,

chunks.en: and the king brings a goat.
chunks.st: and the king brings a goat,
chunks.stMore: as he would have done during his reign.

summary: If the Kohen Gadol stepped down and then sinned, he still brings a bull. But a king who stepped down and then sinned is like a regular person.

chunks.en: If the anointed Kohen stepped down from being Kohen Gadol
chunks.st: In the case of an anointed priest who moved on from his anointment

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, who was anointed with special oil.

chunks.en: and afterwards sinned,
chunks.st: and thereafter sinned,

chunks.en: and the same for a king who stepped down from his greatness
chunks.st: and likewise the king who moved on from his prominence

words.note: The Nasi here means the king.

chunks.en: and afterwards sinned,
chunks.st: and thereafter sinned,

chunks.en: the anointed Kohen brings a bull,
chunks.st: an anointed priest brings a bull,
chunks.stMore: which he would have brought while he was High Priest,

chunks.en: but the king is like a regular person.
chunks.st: and the status of the king is like that of a commoner [kehedyot].

words.note: Someone who is not a king or Kohen Gadol.

summary: If someone sinned before he became king or Kohen Gadol, he brings the korban of a regular person. The king is called Nasi because only Hashem is above him.

chunks.en: If they sinned before they were appointed,
chunks.st: If a king or High Priest sinned before they were appointed,

chunks.en: and afterwards they were appointed,
chunks.st: and thereafter they were appointed,

chunks.en: they are like regular people.
chunks.st: the status of these people is like that of commoners;
chunks.stMore: they bring the sin-offering of an individual.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: אִם נוֹדַע לָהֶם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַנּוּ,
chunks.en: if they found out about the sin before they were appointed,
chunks.st: If it became known to them, before they were appointed
chunks.stMore: as king or High Priest, that they had sinned,

chunks.en: they must bring a korban. But if after they were appointed,
chunks.st: they are liable to bring the sin-offering of an individual, but if it became known to them after they were appointed as king or High Priest

words.en: and from when they were appointed

chunks.en: they are free. And who is the Nasi?
chunks.st: they are completely exempt. Who is the nasi?

chunks.en: This is the king,
chunks.st: This is a king,

chunks.en: because it says, "And he does one
chunks.st: as it is stated: “When a nasi sins, and performs any one

chunks.en: of all the mitzvos of Hashem his God,"
chunks.st: of all the mitzvot of the Lord his God that shall not be performed, unwittingly, and he is guilty” (Leviticus 4:22),

chunks.en: a Nasi who has no one over him
chunks.st: referring to one who has only

chunks.en: except Hashem his God.
chunks.st: the Lord his God over him and no other authority. That is only the king.

summary: This mishnah explains who the anointed Kohen is, and the few differences between different kinds of Kohen Gadol. In most halachos they are all the same.

chunks.en: And who is the anointed Kohen?
chunks.st: And who is the anointed priest?

words.note: The Kohen Gadol who was anointed.

chunks.en: The one anointed with the special anointing oil,
chunks.st: It is the High Priest who is anointed with the anointing oil,

words.note: Special oil that Moshe made to anoint the Kohanim.

chunks.en: not the one who became Kohen Gadol by wearing the extra clothes.
chunks.explain: Later, the oil was hidden, so the Kohen Gadol began by wearing his special clothes.
chunks.st: not the High Priest consecrated by donning multiple garments,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one who served after the anointing oil had been sequestered, toward the end of the First Temple period.

chunks.he: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן הַמָּשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
chunks.en: The only difference between the Kohen anointed with the oil
chunks.st: The difference between a High Priest anointed with the anointing oil

chunks.en: and the one with the extra clothes is the bull
chunks.st: and one consecrated by donning multiple garments unique to the High Priest is only that the latter does not bring the bull

chunks.en: that is brought for all the mitzvos.
chunks.explain: Only the anointed one brings a bull for a mistaken ruling.
chunks.st: that comes for the transgression of any of the mitzvot.

chunks.he: וְאֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר,
chunks.en: And the only difference between the Kohen Gadol who is serving and one who stepped down
chunks.st: And the difference between a High Priest currently serving in that capacity and a former High Priest who had temporarily filled that position while the High Priest was unfit for service

chunks.he: אֶלָּא פַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה.
chunks.en: is the bull of Yom Kippur and the tenth of an eifah.
chunks.explain: The tenth of an eifah is a flour korban the Kohen Gadol brings every day.
chunks.st: is only with regard to the bull brought by the High Priest on Yom Kippur and the tenth of an ephah meal-offering brought by the High Priest daily.
chunks.stMore: Each of these offerings is brought only by the current High Priest, and not by a former High Priest.

chunks.he: זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין בַּעֲבוֹדַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
chunks.en: Both are the same in the avodah of Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: Both this High Priest currently serving and that former High Priest are equal with regard to performing the rest of the Yom Kippur service,

chunks.en: and both are commanded to marry a besulah,
chunks.st: and they are both commanded with regard to marrying a virgin (see Leviticus 21:13),

words.note: A girl who was never married before.

chunks.en: and both may not marry a widow,
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for both to marry a widow (see Leviticus 21:14),

chunks.en: and they do not become tamei for their relatives who passed away,
chunks.st: and they may not render themselves impure with impurity imparted by a corpse even in the event that one of their relatives dies (see Leviticus 21:11),

chunks.en: and they do not let their hair grow long when mourning,
chunks.st: and they may not grow their hair long

chunks.en: and they do not tear their clothes,
chunks.st: and they may not rend their garments as expressions of mourning (see Leviticus 21:10),

chunks.en: and when they pass away, the one who killed by accident goes back home.
chunks.explain: He goes home from the city of refuge where he had to stay.
chunks.st: and when they die they restore the unwitting murderer to his home from the city of refuge (see Numbers 35:25).

words.note: Someone who killed a person by accident.

summary: This mishnah teaches how a Kohen Gadol mourns differently from a regular Kohen: how he tears his clothing, and whether he may bring korbanos on the day a close relative passed away.

chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol tears his clothes from below,
chunks.st: A High Priest rends his garments from below when he is in mourning,

chunks.en: and a regular Kohen from above.
chunks.st: and an ordinary priest rends his garments from above like a non-priest.

chunks.he: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מַקְרִיב אוֹנֵן וְלֹא אוֹכֵל,
chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol may bring korbanos as an onen, but may not eat from them.
chunks.explain: An onen is a mourner on the day a close relative passed away.
chunks.st: A High Priest sacrifices offerings as an acute mourner, i.e., on the day of the death of one of his close relatives, but he may not eat from those offerings.

words.note: A mourner on the day a close relative passed away.

chunks.en: But a regular Kohen may not bring korbanos and may not eat.
chunks.st: And an ordinary priest who is an acute mourner neither sacrifices offerings nor eats from those offerings.

summary: This mishnah teaches what comes first: something that happens more often comes first, and something holier comes first. So the Kohen Gadol's bull comes before the community's bull.

chunks.en: Whatever happens more often than another
chunks.st: Any mitzva that is more frequent than another mitzva

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes that other mitzva
chunks.stMore: if the opportunity to fulfill one of them coincides with an opportunity to fulfill the other.

chunks.en: And whatever is holier than another
chunks.st: And anyone who is more sanctified than another

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes that other person.

chunks.en: If the bull of the anointed Kohen and the bull of the community are both waiting,
chunks.st: If the bull of the anointed priest and the bull of the congregation, which are brought for absence of awareness of the matter, are pending,

chunks.en: the bull of the anointed Kohen comes before the bull
chunks.st: the bull of the anointed priest precedes the bull

chunks.en: of the community in all its steps.
chunks.st: of the congregation in all its actions, i.e., its sacrificial rites.

summary: This mishnah teaches who we help first, a man or a woman, in different kinds of trouble.

chunks.he: הָאִישׁ קוֹדֵם לָאִשָּׁה לְהַחֲיוֹת וּלְהָשִׁיב אֲבֵדָה.
chunks.en: A man comes before a woman to save his life and to give back a lost thing.
chunks.st: The man precedes the woman when there is uncertainty with regard to which of them to rescue or to return a lost item to first.

chunks.en: And a woman comes before a man to be given clothing,
chunks.st: And the woman precedes the man with regard to which of them to provide with a garment first,

chunks.en: and to be freed from captivity.
chunks.st: or to release from captivity first,
chunks.stMore: due to the concern that she will be raped.

chunks.en: When both are in danger of being harmed,
chunks.st: When they are both subject to degradation,
chunks.stMore: i.e., there is also concern that the man will be raped in captivity,

chunks.en: the man comes first.
chunks.st: the release of the man precedes the release of the woman.

summary: This mishnah lists who comes first by family: a Kohen, a Levi, a Yisrael, and so on. But Torah learning is greater than all of it.

chunks.en: A Kohen comes before a Levi,
chunks.st: A priest precedes a Levite.

chunks.en: a Levi before a Yisrael,
chunks.st: A Levite precedes an Israelite.

chunks.en: a Yisrael before a mamzer,
chunks.st: An Israelite precedes a son born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzer],

words.note: A mamzer is someone whose family line keeps him from marrying into most families.

chunks.en: a mamzer before a Givoni,
chunks.st: and a mamzer precedes a Gibeonite,

words.note: From the Givonim, who joined the Jews in Yehoshua's time.

chunks.en: a Givoni before a ger,
chunks.st: and a Gibeonite precedes a convert,

words.note: Someone who was not born Jewish and became Jewish.

chunks.en: and a ger before a freed eved.
chunks.st: and a convert precedes an emancipated slave.

words.note: A servant who was set free.

chunks.en: When is this? When they are all equal.
chunks.explain: Equal in how much Torah they know.
chunks.st: When do these halakhot of precedence take effect? In circumstances when they are all equal in terms of wisdom.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
chunks.en: But if a mamzer is a talmid chacham,
chunks.st: But if there were a mamzer who is a Torah scholar

words.note: A talmid chacham is a Torah scholar.

chunks.en: and a Kohen Gadol knows no Torah,
chunks.st: and a High Priest who is an ignoramus,

words.note: An am ha'aretz is someone who has not learned Torah.

chunks.en: the mamzer who is a talmid chacham comes before
chunks.st: a mamzer who is a Torah scholar precedes

chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol who knows no Torah.
chunks.st: a High Priest who is an ignoramus,
chunks.stMore: as Torah wisdom surpasses all else.
